entry: Physical contest in which a bullfighter subdues, immobilizes or kills a bull under set rules or cultural conventions. The best-known form, Spanish-style bullfighting, is practiced in [[Spain]], a few of Spain's former American colonies, parts of the [[Philippines]], [[Portugal]] and southern [[France]]. The bout ends with the matador killing the bull with a sword after passes with a *muleta*. The practice may descend from prehistoric bull worship and sacrifice in Mesopotamia and the Mediterranean region. It is controversial over animal welfare, funding and religion. Some forms are considered a blood sport, while in some countries, such as Spain, it is defined as an art form or cultural event. It is illegal in most countries but remains legal in most areas of Spain and Portugal and in some [[Latin America|Latin American]] countries. In [[Colombia]] it is being phased out, with a full ban due to take effect in 2027.

Use of force, aggression, coercion or threats to abuse, dominate or intimidate others. It is a subcategory of [[Aggression|aggressive behavior]] with hostile intent, typically repeated over time and involving a perceived imbalance of physical or social power. It may be carried out by an individual or by a group, a practice known as mobbing. It is divided into four basic types of abuse: psychological (also called emotional or relational), verbal, physical and cyber, though an encounter can fall into more than one. A bullying culture can develop wherever people interact, including in [[School|schools]], families and workplaces. A 2019 study in *The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health* found a relationship between social media use by girls and increased exposure to bullying. In the United Kingdom there is no legal definition of bullying, while some U.S. states have laws specifically against it.

Any of over 250 species of hairy, social [[Bee|bees]] in the genus *Bombus*. Bumblebees are found mainly in the [[Northern Hemisphere]], with a few lowland tropical species in South America. Most form colonies headed by a single queen. Colonies are smaller than those of [[Honey bee|honey bees]], growing to as few as 50 individuals. Cuckoo bumblebees are brood parasites that invade the nests of other species, kill the resident queens and lay their own eggs. Nest-making bumblebees carry [[Pollen|pollen]] in pollen baskets on their hind legs and are important agricultural pollinators. Their decline in Europe, North America and Asia is a concern, caused by habitat loss, the mechanization of agriculture and [[Pesticide|pesticides]].

Founder of the First Turkic Khaganate. Bumin was the eldest son of the [[Göktürks|Göktürk]] chieftain Ashina Tuwu and initially served as chieftain of the Göktürks under the Rouran Khaganate. After the Rouran *khagan* Yujiulü Anagui refused his request for a princess and called him a "blacksmith slave," Bumin killed the emissary, severed relations with the Rouran and emerged as leader of the revolt against them. In 551 he received a Western Wei princess, Princess Changle, in marriage. Chinese records call him Tumen; scholars consider the two names to refer to the same person, though they do not match phonetically.

American crime boss in Harlem, [[New York City]]. Known as Bumpy, Ellsworth Raymond Johnson began as an enforcer for numbers queen Madame Stephanie St. Clair and later controlled much of Harlem's rackets, forming an alliance with the Mafia after Dutch Schultz's 1935 murder. Sentenced in 1952 to 15 years for a [[Heroin|heroin]] conspiracy, he served most of the term at Alcatraz. He died of a heart attack while under federal drug indictment.

Professional [[Association football|association football]] league and the highest level of the German league system. Founded in 1962 and first played in 1963–64, it has 18 teams that operate promotion and relegation with the 2. Bundesliga. Bayern Munich has won 34 of the 63 titles, including 11 consecutive seasons from 2013 to 2023. Bundesliga clubs have won eight [[UEFA Champions League]] titles.

Upward force exerted by a fluid, opposing the weight of a partly or fully immersed object. [[Pressure]] in a fluid increases with depth, so the pressure at the bottom of a submerged object exceeds that at its top, producing a net upward force. [[Archimedes' principle]] states that the force equals the weight of the fluid displaced by the object. An object with a [[Density|density]] greater than the surrounding fluid sinks, while a less dense object floats. Buoyancy is the most common driving force of [[Convection|convection]] currents, such as the spontaneous separation of air and water or of oil and water. The center of buoyancy is the center of gravity of the displaced fluid.

Atypical antidepressant, sold as Wellbutrin among other brands. Formerly called amfebutamone, it is a norepinephrine–[[Dopamine|dopamine]] reuptake inhibitor, indicated for [[Major depressive disorder]], seasonal affective disorder and [[Smoking cessation]]. Unlike many [[Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor|selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors]], it usually does not cause sexual dysfunction or weight gain. Its immediate-release form carries a higher risk of seizure than many other antidepressants. It was first approved in the United States in 1985.

American [[Fast food|fast-food]] chain specializing in [[Hamburger|hamburgers]], headquartered in Miami-Dade County, Florida. Founded in 1953 as Insta-Burger King, it added the Whopper in 1957, which became its signature product. In late 2010, 3G Capital of Brazil acquired a majority stake for US$3.26 billion, and the company was eventually merged with Tim Hortons under Restaurant Brands International. As of December 31, 2018, it had 17,796 outlets in 100 countries, 99.7% privately owned and operated.

Purplish, dark-red color. The name comes from the Burgundy wine of [[France]], and the first recorded use of *burgundy* as a color name in English was in 1881. In RGB terms, burgundy is 50% red, 0% green and 13% blue. Akin shades include wine red, [[Crimson]], maroon and mulberry. A brighter tone, vivid burgundy, is used in cosmetology for coloring [[Hair|hair]].

Method of final disposition in which a dead body is placed in the ground or in a structure such as a mausoleum; also called interment or inhumation. Some archaic and [[Early modern human|early modern humans]] buried their dead, and intentional burial with grave goods may be among the earliest detectable forms of religious practice. [[Neanderthal|Neanderthals]] used shallow graves furnished with stone tools and animal bones, at sites including Shanidar in Iraq, Kebara Cave in Israel and Krapina in Croatia, although some scholars argue that such burials may have been for secular reasons. Burial methods include natural or green burial, embalming or mummification, and containers such as shrouds, coffins and burial vaults. Alternatives include [[Cremation|cremation]], burial at sea and cryopreservation.

Megatall [[Skyscraper|skyscraper]] in [[Dubai]], [[United Arab Emirates]], and the world's tallest structure. Designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, it has a total height of 829.8 m (2,722 ft) and has been the tallest building since its complete inauguration in 2011, surpassing Taipei 101. Construction began in 2004. Its design is derived from [[Islamic architecture]], and a buttressed central core and wings support its height. The tower is named after Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the former UAE president, whose government gave financial support when developer Emaar Properties faced difficulties during the [[Great Recession]]. It has 57 [[Elevator|elevators]] and 8 escalators.

Landlocked country in [[West Africa]] (pop., 2024: 23,286,000). Its capital and largest city is [[Ouagadougou]]. The Mossi people, the largest ethnic group, settled the area in the 11th and 13th centuries. [[France]] colonized the area in 1896, and it gained independence in 1960 as the Republic of Upper Volta. Renamed Burkina Faso in 1984 by [[Thomas Sankara]], the country has experienced repeated coups, including two in 2022. It remains one of the least developed countries, with a GDP of $16.226 billion in 2022, and has reserves of gold, manganese, copper and limestone.

Literary, dramatic or musical work intended to cause laughter by caricaturing serious works or by ludicrous treatment of their subjects. The word, from Italian *burlesco*, has been used in English since the late 17th century. [[Alexander Pope]]'s *The Rape of the Lock* and Samuel Butler's *Hudibras* are contrasting examples of literary burlesque, and [[Miguel de Cervantes]] ridiculed medieval romance in his satirical works. An example of musical burlesque is [[Richard Strauss]]'s 1890 *Burleske* for piano and orchestra. In the United States the term later denoted variety-show performances, popular from the 1860s to the 1940s, with bawdy comedy and female striptease. Interest in the form has revived since the 1990s.

Tibeto-Burman language, the official language and lingua franca of [[Myanmar]]. It is the native language of the Bamar, the country's largest ethnic group, and in 2019 was spoken by 42.9 million people, including 32.9 million as a first language. A 2023 World Bank survey found that 80% of the country's population speaks Burmese. It is tonal, largely monosyllabic and agglutinative, with subject–object–verb word order, and belongs to the Lolo-Burmese grouping of the [[Sino-Tibetan languages|Sino-Tibetan]] family. Its alphabet descends from a Brahmic script. The standard dialect originates in the [[Irrawaddy River]] valley and is typified by the [[Yangon]] dialect.

Injury to [[Skin|skin]] or other tissue caused by heat, electricity, chemicals, friction or [[Ionizing radiation|ionizing radiation]]. First-degree burns affect only the superficial skin layer, appearing red without blisters. Second-degree burns extend into part of the underlying skin and are often very painful, while third-degree burns involve the full thickness of the skin and are often painless. Fourth-degree burns also injure muscle, tendons or bone. Most burns are thermal, from scalding liquids or fire, and the most common complications involve [[Infection|infection]]. Cooling with tap water may ease pain, while full-thickness burns usually require skin grafting. The World Health Organization estimated that about 163,000 people died from fire, heat and hot substances in 2023, most of them in the developing world, particularly [[Southeast Asia]].

Nigerian singer, songwriter and record producer. After his debut album *L.I.F.E* (2013), he signed with Atlantic Records in 2017, and *Twice as Tall* (2020) won Best World Music Album at the 63rd Annual [[Grammy Awards]]. *Love, Damini* (2022) became the highest debut Nigerian album on the Billboard 200. In May 2026 he collaborated with [[Shakira]] on the 2026 World Cup song "Dai Dai", which reached number one in over thirty countries.

Annual experimental event held in the Black Rock Desert of [[Nevada]]. Participants create all of its art, activities and events, which culminate in the burning of a large wooden effigy called the Man. It originated on June 22, 1986, on Baker Beach in San Francisco and has been held in Nevada since 1990. Organized by the nonprofit Burning Man Project, it is guided by ten principles, including radical self-reliance and leaving no trace. In 2019, 78,850 people participated.

City in northwestern [[Turkey]] and administrative center of Bursa Province (pop., 2025: around 2.5 million). Known in antiquity as Prusa, it was captured from the Byzantines in 1326 and served as the capital of the early [[Ottoman Empire]] until the 1360s. The mausoleums of the early Ottoman sultans are located in Bursa, and the city has thermal baths, Ottoman mansions and palaces. By the mid-6th century it was known for [[Silk|silk]] textile manufacturing. Bursa is also a center of Turkey's automotive production, and nearby Mount Uludağ has a [[Skiing|ski]] resort. It has been described as historically a safe haven for [[LGBTQ people]].

American actor and film producer. After serving in [[World War II]], he landed a Broadway role, and his appearance in *The Killers* (1946) with [[Ava Gardner]] launched his film career. He won the Academy Award for Best Actor for *Elmer Gantry* (1960) and was a four-time nominee in that category. His films include *From Here to Eternity* (1953), *Sweet Smell of Success* (1957) and *Birdman of Alcatraz* (1962).

American actor and director. After his breakthrough in *Deliverance* (1972), he starred in *Smokey and the Bandit* (1977) and other box-office hits, and was voted the world's most bankable movie star from 1978 to 1982. He won a Golden Globe Award and a Primetime Emmy Award for the sitcom *Evening Shade* (1990–1994). He was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for *Boogie Nights* (1997), directed by [[Paul Thomas Anderson]].

Landlocked country in [[East Africa]], located in the [[Great Rift Valley]]. Its political capital is Gitega and its largest city Bujumbura. Gaining independence in 1962, it initially retained the monarchy and became a one-party republic after a 1966 coup. A 1972 genocide targeted its Hutu population, and Melchior Ndadaye, the first Hutu president, was assassinated in a coup attempt three months after his 1993 election, provoking a 12-year civil war. The 2000 Arusha Agreement was largely integrated into a new constitution in 2005, but the Hutu-led CNDD–FDD party has dominated since then and is widely accused of authoritarian governance. Burundi is the poorest country in the world by nominal GDP per capita, and in 2019 just 13.4% of its population lived in urban areas.

Motor vehicle carrying significantly more passengers than a [[Car|car]] or [[Van|van]], but fewer than [[Rail transport|rail transport]]. Buses typically carry 30 to 100 passengers, and most are used in [[Public transport|public transport]], though they also serve school transport, private hire and tourism. The word derives from the Latin *omnibus*, meaning for all, a name that originated with a horse-drawn service begun in 1823 near [[Nantes]], France. Steam buses followed in the 1830s, electric trolleybuses in 1882 and internal combustion motor buses in 1895.

Second most populous city in [[South Korea]], after [[Seoul]] (pop., 2024: over 3.3 million), and the economic, cultural and educational center of the southeast. Its port is the country's busiest and the world's sixth-largest container port, and the surrounding Southeastern Maritime Industrial Region is South Korea's largest industrial area. Busan hosted an APEC summit in 2005 and the 2002 Asian Games and FIFA World Cup matches. It was added to the [[UNESCO]] Creative Cities Network as a City of Film in December 2014. Home to the Shinsegae Centum City, the world's largest department store.

Large terrestrial [[Bird|bird]] of the family Otididae, including floricans and korhaans. Bustards live mainly in dry grassland and [[Steppe|steppe]] regions, range from 40 to 150 cm in length, and 26 species are currently recognized. They are omnivorous, eating seeds, leaves, fruit, small [[Vertebrate|vertebrates]] and [[Invertebrate|invertebrates]]. The kori bustard and great bustard (*Otis tarda*) are frequently cited as the world's heaviest flying birds. In most species males are substantially larger than females, while in the floricans the female is slightly larger. Bustards nest on the ground, and most prefer to run or walk rather than fly.
